notes.text: The author complains of the absence of a functor from ens. (semi) simpliciaux to n-groupoïdes, describes the geometric intuition as very clear, and says a theory omitting it would seem canularesque to him. These are the author’s assessments, not verified mathematical results.

The proposal begins Peut-être en essayant d’écrire and uses voudrait, arriverait-on, soit … soit, and à la rigueur. The Noël-list aside qualifies the proposed list of notions and relations. The author suggests an axiomatic description might yield an explicit construction or permit an existence-and-uniqueness theorem. The awkward visible sequence qui, soit … soit qui permette is preserved, without grammatical or mathematical repair.

The second paragraph explicitly says n’ayant pas compris l’idée de Segal and je ne vois pas comment tu définis les n-cat. de Picard, followed by mais peu importe. The strict-Picard requirement is what the author says he asks of them, and D’accord ? is a question to the recipient.

The proposed target is an inserted (n+1)-catégorie, followed by a distinct baseline (n+1)-équivalente, compared with complexes de chaines de longueur n. Both dimensions and the final n were inspected independently. No proof, theorem validation, dimension argument, counterexample search, or external mathematical comparison was performed; checks is therefore empty.

Continuation page of a handwritten letter, author number 2 at top, archive pencil foliation 147 at lower left. There is no date, salutation, signature, separate marginal note, display, diagram, drawing, typed layer, or stamp on this sheet. The end Je te remercie continues beyond the page.

Three interlinear additions are present: essayant d’, qui permette, and (n+1)-. The relations/notions correction crosses the physical line boundary; both source boxes are recorded. Two overwritten words preserve uncertain earlier layers. H’s editorial note acknowledges some corrections, but its assertion that the écri-ending was not rewritten is stronger than the surviving ambiguous ink permits. C’s possible re is retained with doubt.

Five letter/word doubts remain in the crowded corrections and the donne/donner ending. A sixth doubt is a faint possible point after Comme, omitted by both witnesses; its intentional status is uncertain. The initial barred m, final dont on, final qui, essayant d’, and pronoun ils are decided from visible strokes.

Insertion guide strokes are recorded as placement, not underlining. Connected g descenders under words such as géométrique, rigueur and longueur are not independent emphasis rules. The possible point after Comme is not silently equated with punctuation; its alternative is a surface/copying speck.

Only the assigned packet, brief, conventions, preamble, notation snapshot and the three designated images were consulted. No OCR, web, external references, other pages, other readers, main decisions, compilation, or delegation was used. One failed image-tool invocation returned no image; its successful retry is the sole actual view of crop 02.
